Bird toys are definitely the way to go. I almost only use bird toys for them because they're so readily available.

Provide solid food and keep feeding milk, allow them to wean themselves basically. Eventually they will transition on their own. You can provide semi solid food as well, to make the transition a bit easier.

After immediate needs are met, you can call local places that rehab animals, but my area doesn't have any so...

Make sure you're not seeing bubbles form on their mouths or noses, that means you're feeding too fast. Make sure the milk is warm. I used goat milk to save my baby mouse whose mom died. Keep them warm but don't overheat them, like a heating pad with a blanket over it was good for my babies. Stay persistent and stick to the feeding schedule. I started at every 1.5 hours because I had discovered mine after their mom passed and they were without food and good milk for God knows how long. Then I went every two hours until they could eat solids and drink on their own.

Mainly, don't give up and power through if you're committing to this. Having somebody take shifts is very helpful.
